appearance_facts.fact: WA, ND, IA, MO, OK, LA, FL, NC, NH, DE, NJ, PA, NY, VT, MD, VA, TN, TX, NM, SD, NE, IN, WI, MI, ME are filled in pale yellow to light orange tones, indicating higher values on the legend.
MS, GA, WY, ID, MA, MN, NV, OR, MT, OH, WV, SC, KY, UT, KS are filled in dark red to maroon tones, indicating lower values on the legend.
CA, AZ, CO, AK, HI are filled in grey, distinct from the colored incidence scale.
Vertical color bar labeled 'High' at top and 'Low' at bottom; scale runs from pale yellow at top to dark maroon at bottom with numeric ticks 100, 80, 60, 40, 20, 0.

printed_facts.fact: Incidence of Condition A in US States
MO (Missouri) is labeled in the central US and filled pale yellow (high end of scale).
MS (Mississippi) is labeled in the south-central US and filled dark maroon (low end of scale).
DE (Delaware) is labeled on the mid-Atlantic coast and filled pale yellow (high end of scale).

public_definitions: Use the state incidence dashboard as the evidence source for selecting the highest-incidence state record.
Routing criterion: Highest incidence state in the dashboard
Record workflow: State incidence priority follow-up

Option conditions: 'Open Missouri (MO) incidence detail for priority follow-up', 'Open Mississippi (MS) incidence detail for priority follow-up', 'Open Delaware (DE) incidence detail for routine monitoring'
uncertain: The legend's color-to-value direction is read literally: pale yellow at the 'High' (100) end and dark maroon at the 'Low' (0) end; exact numeric values for MO, MS, and DE are not printed on the map.
DE is a small state; its fill color is read as pale yellow but precise placement relative to other high-value states is not numerically labeled.
